messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: synthetic_canary_us-west-2 latency_p95 > 2.0s for model-v2 (probe: canary-gen-01). Count=8 in 10m, flapping. Auto-escalation to on-call.

Sara V: On it, I'm taking first touch. Do we know if this is a real customer impact or probe noise?

Omar K: Looks like time-correlated spikes around 02:03-02:08 UTC. Quick check: any deploys in the window? @Matt R can you confirm?

Matt R: No deploys in that window. I'm seeing a queue backlog on the frontend LB for a few minutes. P95 at the proxy rose to 1.8s then backend tokenization spiked. Logs: ```
[02:03:12] token-service WARNING input-size=4096 request_id=abc123 latency=1.9s
[02:04:01] token-service ERROR downstream-timeout request_id=def456
```

Li Chen: Might be amplification in synthetic workload. The canary runs at 60s cadence and we recently added an extra path hitting larger context. If multiple probes run concurrently they push burst over our tokenization pool.

Sara V: Ok. Immediate mitigation: can we throttle the synth job frequency and debounce alerting so customers don't get paged? I want to avoid an actual customer page if it's just synthetic noise.

Omar K: Agreed. Two actions: 1) throttle canary frequency from 60s -> 300s; 2) mute the specific alert rule for 30m while we confirm. I'll add a temporary silence.

Li Chen: Command to silence specific alert group: ```bash
# silence synthetic canary latency for 30m
curl -s -XPOST http://alertmanager-api/api/v1/silences -d '{"matchers":[{"name":"alertname","value":"SyntheticCanaryLatency","isRegex":false}],"startsAt":"2026-03-15T02:10:00Z","endsAt":"2026-03-15T02:40:00Z","createdBy":"oncall","comment":"temporary mute while throttling canaries"}' | jq .
```

Matt R: Silence is up. Also increased debounce on the alert from 2 to 8 occurrences in 5m so transient spikes don't page. I pushed the change to alerting config via our tooling: `redwood-ops apply alerting/canary_latency.yaml`

Sara V: Throttled canaries too. I edited the scheduler to 300s for canary-gen-01 and canary-gen-02. Patch: ```yaml
canaries:
  - id: canary-gen-01
    cadence: 300s
    paths: ["/generate", "/generate-large"]
```

Omar K: Watching metrics. Early signs: token-service queue cleared, p95 back to baseline at ~0.25s. No customer-facing errors in the last 5m.

Julia P: I'm next on-call at 03:00 UTC, please handoff with a summary and actions.

Sara V: Handoff summary for @Julia P:
- Incident origin: synthetic canary amplified tokenization load due to recent addition of large context path.
- Impact: probe-induced latency spikes, no confirmed customer errors.
- Mitigations applied: throttled canary cadence 60s -> 300s, created 30m silence for SyntheticCanaryLatency, increased alert debounce to reduce pages.
- Follow-ups: create a dedicated canary dashboard tile (qps, p95, in-flight queue, probe overlap), add runbook step to coordinate probe config changes, consider moving heavy path to separate canary instance.

Omar K: I've opened a short ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4521 "Canary - split heavy path + dashboard + threshold tuning" with labels incident, canary, followup. Assigning to Li & Matt for evaluation.

Li Chen: Proposed longer-term changes:
- Change default canary cadence for heavy-context probes to 5m.
- Add jitter to start times to avoid burst overlap.
- Add a preflight check that refuses probe if tokenization pool usage > 70%.

Matt R: For alert tuning: change SyntheticCanaryLatency rule to use sustained window (e.g., p95 > 2s for 5m) instead of single-eval events. Also add a scoreboard metric for probe-origin so we can filter synthetic noise.

Julia P: Thanks. I'll take ownership of the follow-up ticket during my shift and ensure docs/runbook updated. Handoff notes added to the ticket.

Sara V: Quick customer impact check: I ran the customer-error tracer for the time window; no increase in 5xx from production routes. Confident this was noisy.

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Handoff acknowledged. Next on-call: Julia P (03:00-11:00 UTC).

Omar K: Post-incident actions before close: 1) roll out dashboard tile (priority P2), 2) implement probe jitter and cadence defaults (P1), 3) update alert rule to sustained-window (P1), 4) postmortem doc with timeline and owner (P2).

Sara V: TL;DR - nothing customer-visible, synths caused the blip, temporary throttle + alert mute fixed noise. We'll follow up with config and alert policy changes. :thumbsup:

Julia P: I'll run the postmortem and ping product if any customer-facing risk pops up. Leaving these notes in the ticket and on the runbook. :wave:

incident-bot: Incident resolved for synthetic_canary_us-west-2. Auto-close pending if no reoccurrence in 1h.

end of thread
